thread:
incident-bot: ALERT — dp-acme-prod GPU capacity critical (98%) for 12m; queue length 720. Paging oncall...

Elia (oncall): ACK. Jumping in. Collecting traces and load profiles. @Liam I'll handoff once stable.

Elia (oncall): Metrics snapshot: pool GPUUtil=98.5%, inflight requests ~720, 99p latency 8.2s. Autoscaler made 4 scale attempts; last error: `QuotaExceeded: request 12, quota 0 in us-west1-c`.

Sara (RuntimeEng): Runtime shows many retry loops and KV misses. Autoscaler trace indicates preferred zone us-west1-c failed; fallback policy not triggering. We see many cold starts.

Marc (Ops-SRE): Tenant: Acme Pharma (acme-prod-01). Reserved GPUs 32. Burst policy disabled by default. Shared burst pool `dedicated-burst-east` has 10 preemptible and 2 on-demand available.

Andrew (Acct): I can authorize emergency burst for up to 12 GPUs for 90 minutes. Prefer we inform CS and get their ok before we attach.

Julia (CS): I'll prepare a customer-facing interim message: short statement that we're applying temporary capacity and mitigating impact; include expected time to stable (~30-45m).

Elia (oncall): Following runbook: attempt attach from burst pool, then apply per-tenant throttles and small-batch enforcement; pause any detected bulk cron jobs. Kicking off attach of 8 on-demand GPUs and fallback to preemptible if needed.

Elia (oncall): Command executed:
```
redwoodctl pool attach-gpus --pool dp-acme-prod --from dedicated-burst-east --count 8 --type on-demand
```

orchestrator-bot: job accepted job-10456. Starting allocation.

Sara (RuntimeEng): Note: cross-zone attachment will trigger KV shard movement; expect short 200-400ms spikes while caches populate.

Elia (oncall): Meanwhile applying route-level throttle on heavy embedding routes and enforcing max_batch=8.
PATCH /v1/tenants/acme-prod/rate_limit
{"tokens_per_minute":"150000"}

redwoodctl routes set --tenant acme-prod --route /v1/embeddings --max_batch 8

Marc (Ops-SRE): Allocation progress: 5/8 GPUs attached. Device plugin shows devices online. Queue dropping 720 -> 250.

Liam: CS confirm if there are any customer-side scheduled jobs. Julia?

Julia (CS): Found an erroneous bulk export cron that started earlier; I've paused it and notified their ops.

orchestrator-bot: job-10456 now requiring 3 more GPUs; automatically offering preemptible fallback. Proceeding with 3 preemptible attach.

Elia (oncall): Attaching 3 preemptible. Command:
redwoodctl pool attach-gpus --pool dp-acme-prod --from dedicated-burst-east --count 3 --type preemptible

Marc (Ops-SRE): Attach complete: +11 GPUs total. Pool utilization now 69%. Tail latency now under SLO thresholds.

Sara (RuntimeEng): KV caches warming complete. Observed tail latency drop; 95p back to SLO after ~12m.

Elia (oncall): Creating incident ticket INC-2026-ACME-131. Logging timeline, job-10456, throttle patches, and route changes. Assigning follow-ups.

Elia (oncall): Initial root-cause hypothesis: sudden customer batch spike (mis-scheduled job) plus zone quota exhaustion prevented autoscaler from scaling; autoscaler lacks automatic burst fallback.

Andrew (Acct): Approving the 11 GPU burst for 90 minutes. Billing note: absorb first 30m as credit.

Julia (CS): Message sent to customer. They responded: "Thanks, please share postmortem and confirm billing." I've replied with expected timeline and that we'll follow up.

Sara (RuntimeEng): Follow-ups: autoscaler change to attempt burst attach on placement failure, lower early-warning threshold for queue growth from 500 to 200, add a device-plugin readiness gate in node init.

Marc (Ops-SRE): Opening infra quota ticket INFRA-746 to request additional GPUs for us-west1-c and to add quota monitoring alerts.

Liam: I'll take the overnight monitoring handoff. Handoff_ts 1774005870. Actions: monitor queue, keep throttles for 30m after stable, confirm billing note with Andrew.

Elia (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving channel. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Please add logs to INC-2026-ACME-131.

incident-bot: THREAD UPDATE: mitigated. job-10456 completed. Closing the active paging and moving to monitoring.

Julia (CS): Customer replied again: "Appreciate the quick response. Looking forward to postmortem." I'll schedule the postmortem sync.

Liam: Noted. I'll prepare the postmortem bullets and PR tracker for follow-ups.
